audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Psychology bachelor studies behavior, cognition, development and mental health. Students learn psychological research methods, take specialisation courses and complete a supervised research project. This comparison uses the Dutch-taught route.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR options emphasize broad psychology and research, brain and cognition, or psychology and organizations. Each brings together psychology and complementary disciplines. Leiden provides a more extensive sequence of psychology-specific measurement and professional skills.

curriculum.routeLabel: Dutch-taught Psychology with Cognitive Neuroscience and Social Psychology in Organisations
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC plan includes 20 EC of specialisation, 10 EC of Psychology electives and 30 EC of open study.

componentNotes.later-thesis: Entry requires passing the first year and Multivariate Data Analysis. Assessment includes a research article, oral presentation and the research and collaboration process.
componentNotes.spec-cognitive-neuroscience: One of the selected specialisation courses. Entry requires all 60 EC of year one.
componentNotes.spec-social-organisations: One of the selected specialisation courses. Entry requires all 60 EC of year one.
componentNotes.psychology-electives: This plan uses 10 EC of Psychology electives alongside 20 EC of specialisation.
componentNotes.free-choice: This plan leaves 30 EC for open study. Courses outside the approved offer may require permission.

ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON212.text: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.

source.reviewNote: CP076: full selected description read against current course evidence; accurate bounded official overview. Retain unchanged text, without adding unstated methods or qualifications.

BENECON314.text: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

source.reviewNote: CP076: full selected description read against current course evidence; accurate bounded official overview. Retain unchanged text, without adding unstated methods or qualifications.

BENENTR311.text: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

source.reviewNote: Compared the retained modal with the revised official description. The revision adds promotional wording without changing the substantive account of planning, conducting and analysing market research; the existing concise text remains faithful.

BENGATE101.text: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

source.reviewNote: CP076: full selected description read against current course evidence; accurate bounded official overview. Retain unchanged text, without adding unstated methods or qualifications.

BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD111.text: Introduces self-leadership, leadership theory and emotional intelligence. Students use personality and emotional-intelligence profiles to reflect on group dynamics, study leadership cases, and develop a personal plan with practical goals. Assessment tools support educational reflection, with attention to differences in their scientific support.

BENLEAD112.text: Studies leadership communication through theory, persuasion, emotional intelligence, gender, culture and ethics. Students analyse literary characters, film and speeches, interview a leader, prepare a communication advisory report, and develop an address explaining their own ethical leadership vision.

BENLEAD211.text: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.

BENLEAD312.text: How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.

DISDATA111.text: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.

Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.

Students study utilitarianism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics, alongside Nietzsche, Murdoch and Nagel. Reflection and research essays develop interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.

Students examine animal behaviour, research models, welfare and research ethics, then connect biological rhythms and regulatory behaviour to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders. HCBCOGN311.text: Higher Order Functions deepens knowledge of neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and experimental cognitive neuroscience. Topics include attention, memory, emotion, cognitive control, social cognition, pain and consciousness. An attentional-blink experiment and a team research proposal develop engagement with empirical research, experimental design and ethical reflection.

HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

Students analyse scientific experiments and papers through teaching contributions and a research-based mini-symposium, with additional topics selected with the class.

BENECON312.text: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

finding: Read all 26 external titles and credits, three concepts, all selected course titles and description texts, the official sources, comparison notes, and explicit audience and optional-research references. The record distinguishes psychological assessment from independent professional practice, computation from human perception, and the required Leiden project from optional UCR research.
